question: A visual search task is made harder by adding more items to scan. What happens to interference from an irrelevant flanking letter?
options: It grows, as focus gets stretched
It shrinks, as spare capacity runs out
answer: It shrinks. In Lavie's load theory, a crowded display uses up perception, leaving none to process the distractor. Loading working memory does the reverse: holding digits in mind increased flanker interference in Lavie and colleagues' 2004 study, because control of what gets in weakened. Busy eyes filter well; a busy mind filters badly.
move: Ask which part of the system is busy before predicting what leaks through.
trap: It grows, since a harder task seems to make focus more fragile.
reference: Lavie, Hirst, de Fockert & Viding, Load theory of selective attention and cognitive control, Journal of Experimental Psychology: General, 2004
